source: Ministry of Agriculture training module "ជំនិតកម្មដំណាំខ្នុរសំរាប់កសិកម្ម" (Jackfruit Cultivation Techniques for Agriculture), prepared with participation from the Santisena organization, an elderly people's association, a charitable organization, and the CRS (Catholic Relief Services) agriculture program; content compiled with reference to fruit-tree materials and Prek Leap National School of Agriculture (សាលាជាតិកសិកម្មព្រែកលៀប).
text:
Propagating jackfruit by air-layering (marcotting a branch) produces fruit quickly, within two to three years of planting the rooted cutting, but the resulting tree has a shorter lifespan than a seed-grown tree because its root and trunk development is not as strong.

The method, as shown step by step in the illustrations, is: select a healthy branch no longer than about one meter. Girdle the bark in a ring around the branch, sized to the branch's diameter, and remove the ring of bark. Scrape off the slimy cambium layer underneath and leave the wound to dry for about 15 to 30 minutes. Then wrap the girdled section with a moist rooting medium (such as compost) enclosed in a wrapping material, and tie both ends of the wrapping tightly. Keep the wrapped section watered regularly to stay moist. Once roots are observed to have grown in well, cut the branch below the rooted section and pot it into a bag to continue growing as a new seedling.

The diagrams show this sequence visually: selecting and trimming a leafy branch, preparing/girdling the stem section, wrapping the girdled area in a ball-shaped wrapping tied at the neck, a second tie added further down for security, and finally the rooted cutting shown potted in a bag as an established seedling.
